newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index rises in record trade week.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index rises in record trade week.

text.p: Kuwait shares rose 29.2 points to 2,246.1 in the week to Wednesday with trade volume and value hitting a record high.
Dealers expect the trade to be as active for next week amid indications of economy growth and encouraging performance by many listed firms in the first quarter of 1997.

The daily average for value of traded shares rose to 82 million dinars ($271 million) from 56.2 million. Volume clocked up to a daily average of 288 million shares from 213 million, figures released by the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Thursday show.
"It (trade volume) will be stronger or at least at the same level next week," said a dealer. "There is no reason why it should not be."

Figures published on Thursday show oil exports amounted to 2.997 billion dinars in the nine months to September, almost matching the 3.0 billion dinars total state revenue projection for 1996/97 (July-June) fiscal year.
Many listed firms have reported profit increases in 1996.
Gainers led losers 29-22 while nine were non-movers.
Investment firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 157 million dinars, followed by property firms with 133 million and banks with 57 million.
Kuwait Real Estate, Investment Projects, United Realty, The International Investor and Commercial Bank were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
